948b78f962.title: Three small failures combined to take down Microsoft 365
948b78f962.summary: A hidden defect in Microsoft’s cloud gateway, dormant since July, was to blame for one of the largest outages in the company’s history last week. A preliminary Post-Incident Report (PIR) released by the company outlines how the latent bug, changes in traffic, and reduced server capacity combined to knock much of Microsoft 365 and Exchange infrastructure offline at the end of last week. Microsoft’s report lists the incident’s final status as “a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents.” Microsoft’s preliminary report places the outage between November 12 at 16:20 UTC and November 13 at 16:10 UTC, just under 24 hours total, and additional monitoring remained in place for any affected systems through November 14. The outage started on November 12 and quickly rippled through businesses and public offices that depend on Microsoft’s cloud and email exchange infrastructure. The outage is covered in Microsoft’s incident IDs EX1550543 and MO1550821. You need Microsoft 365 admin credentials to see the full report on the company’s status pages, but Office Watch has reproduced the preliminary report , and the University of Pennsylvania maintains an archive of Microsoft’s service-health updates . Microsoft attributes the outage to three factors. A change deployed to Microsoft’s cloud gateway starting in July created a bug where, under certain conditions, CPU and memory resources could become exhausted and unresponsive. Microsoft contends that the defect was never discovered in pre-release testing because the hardware used was less powerful than some systems already deployed in production, where higher CPU core counts on newer machines apparently contributed to the lockout. The second factor was server load. Microsoft said that “Traffic shifts during standard network maintenance and upgrades exposed a latent bug.” The company keeps two independent gateway systems in place to access Microsoft 365 for resilience. If one system encounters trouble and users can’t get through the front door, the other is opened to keep traffic flowing. According to the report, about 15 hours prior to the outage, traffic from Teams was shifted from the alternate gateway to the primary, where Exchange Online access is maintained. The switchover was a standard fail-safe, but it left the gateway handling more traffic, with a different mix of requests than before. As requests continued to pile up, affected servers exhausted their capacity and refused new connection requests. The traffic…

Lamanna said the software change had operated worldwide for more than three months without problems. a9daf0fb16.title: Microsoft identifies issues leading to global Outlook outage - ABC News
a9daf0fb16.summary: The executive laid out three main issues leading to the outage. Microsoft is apologizing for the mass global Outlook outage last week and identifying the main causes of the problem that spanned across two workdays. In a lengthy social media post Monday morning, a Microsoft executive said a combination of a "latent defect," increased load and lessened server capacity were among the cascading set of issues that led to users across the globe dealing with an outage on the email service. The outage seemingly downed communications across industries last week, with reports of businesses, governments, schools and healthcare providers experiencing communication disruptions. "A latent defect caused servers to become overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions," wrote Charles Lamanna, Executive Vice President of Copilot, Agents, and Platform at Microsoft. The defect came from a fix that was "prepared specifically for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers," he said. Lamana also pointed to "a surge in load" on the networking gateway as a secondary cause of the global outage. The executive highlighted a reduced server capacity as a third primary reason for last week's email service issues, though Lamana said the reduction "had no impact on its own." "Taken together, the increased load and the reduced server capacity, caused the network gateway to encounter the latent bug from July. This caused requests to build up until servers ultimately stopped responding. This occurred during the peak window of traffic in the United States," wrote Lamana. Lamana also explained the extended time period it took to recover from the outage saying, "Recovery took longer than usual because as servers returned to service, they were immediately overwhelmed by waiting traffic and became unresponsive again." "We are deeply sorry for the impact to all our customers and recognize the impact that this has on their normal business & operations," wrote Lamana in the update. 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

7819adf1a0.title: Opinion | What Happens When the Economy Becomes Dependent on AI?
7819adf1a0.summary: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly widespread and embedded in decisions involving credit, investment, production, financial markets and infrastructure, managing the risks associated with its use is becoming more important than ever. The debate surrounding artificial intelligence is no longer confined to its ability to write texts, analyse data or help people perform tasks more quickly. The world has entered a new phase in which AI is gradually moving to the heart of economic decision-making. Banks use it to assess credit applications and detect fraud, companies rely on it for pricing and production, financial markets deploy algorithms for trading, and institutions use it to analyse risks and inform their decisions. The most important economic question, therefore, is no longer simply what artificial intelligence can do, but what happens when the economy itself becomes increasingly dependent on it. This question has become more pressing as AI capabilities advance rapidly and governments and major companies around the world turn greater attention to safety, oversight and governance. This does not mean that artificial intelligence has become a threat to be feared. Quite the opposite: it could become one of the most important drivers of productivity growth over the coming decades by reducing costs, improving business efficiency, enhancing data analysis, accelerating decision-making and facilitating the development of new products and services. However, economic history teaches us that every major productive force also creates new forms of risk. And that is where the real challenge begins. If a single company uses an AI system and that system fails, the company may face an operational problem. But what happens when thousands of companies, banks and institutions depend on the same limited number of models, technology providers or data centres? At that point, the problem shifts from an internal institutional issue to a potential disruption affecting a substantial part of the economy. Artificial intelligence may make the economy more efficient, but it could also make it increasingly dependent on a limited number of companies providing AI models, cloud computing services, semiconductors and data centres. The greater this dependence becomes, the greater the possibility that a problem affecting one of these critical components could spread simultaneously across numerous institutions. It was attended by several ministers, WIPO Director General Daren Tang, the authority’s chairman Hisham Azmy, and officials and experts from intellectual property bodies and the cultural and creative industries in Egypt and abroad. Sessions will cover the future of copyright, the role of intellectual property in supporting cultural and creative industries, and the challenges raised by the use of artificial intelligence to produce and distribute content. Protecting the rights of creators and innovators, he said, went hand in hand with encouraging investment, stimulating scientific research and opening new prospects for the cultural and creative industries. He said Egypt had a large cultural and creative heritage, and the task was to turn it into lasting economic value through an integrated intellectual property system and partnerships with international institutions, led by WIPO. Making the most of intellectual property required coordination across state institutions, links between research output and the needs of industry and investors, and a supportive environment for creators and startups, he added. Tang called for intellectual property systems to adapt to rapid developments in artificial intelligence while preserving the place of the human creator. “Our responsibility is to ensure that copyright continues to serve the creative human spirit, and that human creators in Egypt and around the world remain at the heart of the global intellectual property system,” he said. He praised the steps Egypt had taken to develop its national intellectual property system and the role of the authority. A single national body, he said, gave Egypt an important foundation to make better use of its potential in creativity, research and innovation. 35ec487175.title: California sues OpenAI over Hugging Face, other AI model loss of control
35ec487175.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta on Monday sued artificial intelligence giant OpenAI for allegedly endangering the public by developing advanced AI models without adequate safeguards and monitoring. "OpenAI disregarded public safety, knowingly tested potentially dangerous AI models without proper oversight and safety measures, and misled consumers and the public," Bonta said at a press conference. Bonta cited the "infamous" incident in July, where two OpenAI models broke out of a testing environment, gained unauthorized access to the open internet, and breached the internal systems of open-source developer platform Hugging Face . OpenAI said the models were trying to find information that they could use to cheat on an evaluation, and succeeded. The break-in at Hugging Face, which Nvidia acquired for roughly $13 billion in September. rattled industry researchers and prompted government officials to call for more stringent oversight of the AI industry. On Monday, Bonta said that OpenAI later disclosed to his investigators that it was aware of 80 incidents "involving loss of control and access to third-party networks and websites." "But the company failed to provide the detailed information we requested to evaluate these incidents; this is concerning, and it puts the public at risk," he said. Bonta's suit, filed in state Superior Court in San Francisco, alleges OpenAI violated California's Unfair Competition Law and accuses the company of being a public nuisance as defined by state law. The attorney general told reporters he believed in AI's technological power, and the potential of AI models to "achieve scientific breakthroughs, boost economic growth, guard against cyber attacks, and benefit all Californians." "But AI systems must be developed and designed safely," he said. "The companies that develop these models have a moral and yes, a legal responsibility to keep public safety at the forefront." Bonta's suit comes as Congress has been presented with, but not passed, a comprehensive AI safety bill. AI companies, including OpenAI and Anthropic, along with critics of AI, have called for such legislation on the heels of the Hugging Face break-in and other incidents that have raised concerns about the safety of AI models. Other AI companies, including Anthropic, Meta and Google, have since disclosed incidents where their own models went rogue. But OpenAI is the first to be sued in connection with such incidents by California. OpenAI spokesperson Drew…

8e9eaa53a3.title: California Sues OpenAI Over A.I. Safety Issues
8e9eaa53a3.summary: California sued OpenAI on Monday, accusing the company of putting the public at risk by failing to put appropriate safeguards on its artificial intelligence. The lawsuit is the latest broadside at the company, which — along with other tech industry players — has faced scrutiny over a rush to develop A.I. at the potential expense of consumer safety. In a 31-page lawsuit, filed in San Francisco Superior Court, the state said OpenAI’s lax safeguards led to cyberattacks by its A.I. products during testing, including a breach this year when OpenAI’s agents went rogue and attacked the A.I. start-up Hugging Face’s systems . OpenAI’s behavior created a public nuisance and violated a legal prohibition on unfair or fraudulent business practices, the state said. “OpenAI’s failure to adequately secure and monitor the testing of its highly capable and increasingly powerful A.I. models represents a danger to the public that must be remedied,” the state said in the lawsuit. The move is the latest effort by a state to rein in the power of A.I. companies in the face of growing concerns about the technology’s ability to go rogue. In recent months, A.I. systems produced by major companies including OpenAI, Anthropic and Google have broken out of testing environments designed to keep them from launching cyberattacks on companies and governments, raising alarms. Courts must still decide how legal liability will be applied in those cases. The attorney general’s office is asking a court to force OpenAI to change its business practices and pay civil penalties. According to the state, the hack was the result of OpenAI operating dangerous models in a flawed testing environment. Its failure to adequately rein in its agents, the suit alleges, put the public at risk and violated California’s Unfair Competition Law, which is meant to stop companies from using unfair, unlawful, or fraudulent practices. “The company knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it — this disregard for public safety violated California law,” Bonta said in the announcement. In a press conference announcing the suit, Bonta said tools like OpenAI’s have “enormous potential” but “must be developed and designed safely.” Bonta said the company failed to provide detailed information on dozens of other incidents as well. “Without proper safeguards and monitoring, these models pose a danger to anything connected to the internet,” he said. b7ebb93ddb.title: Google DeepMind researchers verify Signal’s cryptographic core with AlphaProof Code
b7ebb93ddb.summary: Google DeepMind researchers have used AI agents to mathematically prove key security properties of libsignal, the reference implementation of the Signal messaging protocol, connecting cryptographic guarantees to compiled machine code. The work uses AlphaProof Code, a framework that combines human-directed specification writing with teams of agents that generate proofs checked by Lean, a programming language and proof assistant. The researchers describe the result as the first verification of protocol-level security properties for a widely deployed, unmodified cryptographic protocol implementation at this depth. Their paper, published on November 10, examines the code within a defined execution environment and sets out the assumptions and limitations behind its guarantees. Five researchers directed the proof work over four weeks in October 2026. The paper says none of the authors wrote the proof code themselves. The team worked with libsignal’s production Rust code, compiling it within a command-line program for AArch64 Linux, an Arm-based computing environment. The verification covers the protocol’s PQXDH handshake and Triple Ratchet components. The security properties examined include authentication, forward secrecy and post-compromise security, addressing how messages remain protected under specified scenarios involving exposed keys or compromised devices. Much previous protocol analysis has examined mathematical designs, specially written implementations or narrower properties of production software. AlphaProof Code’s research connects security statements to the compiled implementation, where differences between a design and the code that executes it can introduce vulnerabilities. The researchers used two established approaches. A symbolic model treats cryptographic operations abstractly, while a computational model bounds an attacker’s chances of success under assumptions about the underlying cryptography. To test whether the specifications could identify insecure behavior, the team reintroduced two previously fixed libsignal bugs into separate experimental builds. In both cases, the agents produced Lean-checked proofs that the altered implementation violated the symbolic security theorem. These were tests using historical bugs, rather than announcements of newly discovered vulnerabilities in the current software. 19049b375e.title: Google DeepMind launches Gemini Robotics 2.5 with improved dexterity and industrial capabilities
19049b375e.summary: Google DeepMind has introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5, an updated vision-language-action (VLA) model designed to improve robots’ ability to perform complex physical tasks in industrial and everyday environments. Gemini Robotics 2.5 was evaluated across more than 200 tasks, including handling delicate objects, using tools, manipulating flexible materials and performing precision assembly operations. According to Google DeepMind, the model achieved success rates 30 to 100 percent higher than previous versions, depending on the task, while completing operations 20 to 30 percent faster. One of the most significant demonstrations involved Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid robot operating on Mercedes-Benz production lines in Kecskemét, Hungary, and Sindelfingen, Germany. The robots performed automotive kitting, which involves selecting individual components from bulk containers and arranging them into trays for vehicle assembly. Using Gemini Robotics 2.5 to control its arms and hands, alongside Gemini Robotics ER for task planning, Apollo 2 achieved a reported 96 percent success rate during the proof-of-concept program. Jeff Cardenas, co-founder and CEO of Apptronik, says: “This is what we built Apollo for: useful work alongside people in real industrial settings. “Pairing Apollo 2 with Gemini Robotics, we saw the models improve dramatically in just a few weeks of post-training and carry over to Mercedes-Benz production with very little drop-off. This is the foundation for bringing humanoid robots to industrial and commercial environments at scale.” Google DeepMind has also introduced improvements intended to help robots operate safely around obstacles and people. The company reports that new reasoning-based safety controls increased safe task completion by 33 percent around obstacles and 43 percent when people were nearby. Separately, it introduced ASIMOV-Jailbreak, an open-source benchmark designed to evaluate whether robotics AI systems resist instructions that could lead to unsafe actions. Google DeepMind says its Gemini 4 Argon model achieved 99.5 percent resistance in these evaluations, compared with 82 percent for its previous baseline. 2734f46bb6.title: DeepMind Opens Free AI Rain Data: Five-Hour Latency, Claimed Win Over NASA's IMERG-Final
2734f46bb6.summary: Google DeepMind opened two datasets to the public on Friday, Nov. 13, and the headline claim is about rain: PARDIG, a global precipitation record at 0.1° resolution (about 10 km, or 6.2 miles), reaches users roughly five hours after observation , while NASA's research-grade IMERG-Final product takes months. The lab's own paper reports that PARDIG scores higher than both IMERG-Final and IMERG-Early across the thresholds and regions it tested. Any Google Cloud account can download the data, with no access request form , under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0) license. That gives flood modelers, hydrologists and weather developers a same-day global rain reference to train on and to score their own models against. The second release, SatWeave, is an hourly mosaic of geostationary satellite imagery with about one hour of latency , and it supplies the live observations that start WeatherNext 3 every hour. Google labels both products experimental and as-is , and says PARDIG is not an official observation, forecast, watch or warning. The paper went to arXiv on Nov. 10 , three days before the blog post. NASA's IMERG blends data from the GPM satellite constellation into half-hourly global rain estimates , and it comes in three runs. The Early Run arrives about four hours after observation, the Late Run follows after roughly 12 to 14 hours, and the Final Run waits for monthly rain-gauge analysis, which pushes its latency to about three months, with NASA's pages giving figures from 2.5 to 3.5 months. NASA advises researchers to use the Final Run whenever latency allows. PARDIG's near-real-time feed lands in 24 frames every six hours . The newest frame is about two hours old, the oldest about 7.5 to 8 hours, and the average is about five hours. That puts PARDIG in the same latency class as IMERG-Early while, according to the authors, outscoring both Early and Final . DeepMind puts the gain over IMERG-Final at more than 30% in hourly detection skill for light-to-moderate rain. 3dbe83921b.title: The ‘AI Arms Race’ is Unhinged—Both US and Chinese Tech Enthusiasts Know It
3dbe83921b.summary: This week, United States President Donald Trump and China’s President, Xi Jinping, are set to meet on the sidelines of the APEC leaders’ summit in Shenzhen, where leaders are expected to continue their dialogue on artificial intelligence (or, as the White House has dubbed it , “superintelligence”). Questions over the “AI race” between the two countries are swirling amid rapid advances in model capability and related technologies and the stunning downfall of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned amid allegations he had multiple affairs, including with a suspected Chinese agent. But how real is the “race?” The question deserves scrutiny, particularly as it is one of the most significant issues animating US-China relations. When the Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 in 1957, a beach-ball-sized satellite was said to be proof that the US was falling behind. Nearly 70 years later, the same was said about a large language model from a Chinese startup: Deepseek. Within days of its release in late January 2025, Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) told the Senate that it was being called AI’s “Sputnik moment”—a “wake-up call” for a country at risk of losing its lead. On the other side of the Pacific, the Chinese state media outlet, Xinhua News Agency, celebrated R1 as héng kōng chū shì (横空出世), an “arrival out of nowhere” that had placed China in the lead, with the US left following. The same model carried two stories: a threat to be contained, and a rupture to be celebrated. The frame has outlived the model. Each major Chinese release since, including Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 this July, has been met in Washington and Silicon Valley with the same question: Who is winning ? In a recent study , we compared how the US government, Chinese state media and online publics in both countries talked about DeepSeek in the months after its release. The comparison suggests that “who is winning?” is the wrong question. The race is not a fact that the commentary describes, and tech enthusiasts in both countries are aware. The echo of Sputnik is not incidental. In The Closed World , historian of science and technology Paul Edwards showed that Cold War computers were at once machines and metaphors. Military ambitions shaped the technology, and the technology made a world under total surveillance and control seem achievable. AI works the same way today. Recent models from Alibaba Group, Tencent and Moonshot AI have featured scaled-down offensive abilities and improved defensive aptitude. Alibaba unveiled the latest edition of its flagship Qwen series without its weights, the internal settings that shape how a model responds, preventing users from downloading and customising the model’s full version. So-called open-weight systems are attractive to hackers because they can run them locally and configure their settings. DeepSeek’s models have proved particularly popular, while Alibaba’s Qwen series has been ranked among the most downloaded open-weight model families in the world. For months, US AI companies have also been restricting access to their most cyber-capable systems. Anthropic PBC has kept its Mythos Preview model out of general release, making it available to selected organisations for defensive security work. Last month, researchers at CrowdStrike Holdings said hackers used DeepSeek’s model to carry out attacks against organisations in 14 countries. “The cyber ability of models, and soon the bio ability of the models, will reach a threshold where it’s actually possible to do harm,” said Yao Shunyu, Tencent’s chief AI scientist who previously worked for OpenAI, at an event this month in Hong Kong. Qwen 4 Max achieved an initial score of 7.46% across 14,727 sessions, the highest among Chinese participating models. For general users, its visual capabilities may be even more noteworthy. Code Arena’s web development rankings compare AI models’ website-building abilities through one-on-one user voting and a point-based scoring system. f5b8e45b4a.title: Baidu quarterly revenue slips as advertising weakness overshadows AI demand
f5b8e45b4a.summary: China's Baidu reported on Monday quarterly revenue in line with market estimates as weakness in its core advertising division offset strong demand for its AI cloud computing services. US-listed shares of Baidu were down more than 1% in premarket trading. Baidu has been spending heavily to expand in cloud computing as enterprisesboost spending on artificial intelligence. That spending helped lift revenue at Baidu's AI-linked business segment by 37% to 13.2 billion yuan ($1.98 billion). AI cloud infrastructure revenue alone surged 94% to 8.2 billion yuan in the quarter ended September 30. But investors worry that Baidu is falling behind AI rivals such as e-commerce leader Alibaba and startups like DeepSeek and Moonshot due to the lack of major upgrades to its Ernie AI model. Baidu previewed its Ernie 5.5 Flash model this month, touting its capabilities in coding, 3D modelling and content creation. However, the preview attracteda far more muted public response than previous Ernie iterations. Still, performance in AI-related services has helped make up for slowing demand in Baidu's staple online advertising business, where advertisers have tightened budgets as weak consumer spending weighs on the economy. Baidu's online marketing services revenue slid 22% to 11.9 billion yuan in the quarter. The internet search major reported July-September revenue of 30.81 billion yuan ($4.62 billion), versus the 30.86 billion yuan average of 15 analyst estimates compiled by LSEG. Baidu reported an adjusted profit of 6.78 yuan per American Depositary Share, beating estimates of 6.36 yuan, helped by a decline in overall costs. 6bea9f2c7c.title: Meteorological Department Wins International AI Forecasting Challenge in China
6bea9f2c7c.summary: Army evacuates 38th batch of sick children from Gaza for medical treatment Army chief inspects King Hussein bin Ali Brigade Amman, Nov. 16 (Petra) -- The Jordan Meteorological Department (JMD) was selected among the winners of the international MAZU challenge, organized by the China Meteorological Administration in Shanghai to develop innovative forecasting and early warning solutions using artificial intelligence (AI). The JMD submitted a scientific and technical proposal to enhance MAZU, a system created by the China Meteorological Administration, according to a department statement Monday. The proposal combines weather radar data with numerical weather prediction model outputs and adds Arabic-language capability to strengthen weather data analysis, improve forecast accuracy and support early warnings of hazardous weather. JMD Director Raed Khattab said the selection reflects Jordanian specialists’ expertise in meteorology and modern technology and their ability to contribute to advanced AI-based systems. He described it as an important step toward modernizing the Kingdom's forecasting and early warning system. Khattab said JMD specialists and their counterparts at the China Meteorological Administration in Shanghai are working to complete the system's development and adapt it to Jordan's operational needs and its climatic and geographic characteristics. He said development and the start of operations are expected by the end of this year. He said the project takes Jordan’s involvement beyond participation in an international scientific challenge to a practical contribution to an advanced early warning system. Adding Arabic would also help make the system accessible to other Arab countries in the future, he said. Khattab noted that the cooperation reflects the strong scientific and technical partnership between the Jordanian and Chinese meteorological authorities. He said it strengthens the Kingdom's readiness for extreme weather and supports national efforts to reduce disaster risk and protect lives and property. 49594ed570.summary: Army evacuates 38th batch of sick children from Gaza for medical treatment Army chief inspects King Hussein bin Ali Brigade Cairo, Nov. 16 (Petra) -- The League of Arab States and the Global Council for Tolerance and Peace (GCTP) launched the "Arab Declaration for Tolerance and Peace" on Monday during a conference hosted by the Arab League General Secretariat in Cairo to mark the International Day for Tolerance. The declaration aims to promote dialogue and peaceful coexistence, counter extremism, discrimination, and hate speech, and foster a culture of peace across Arab societies. It outlines a framework of commitments and measures to strengthen the role of official religious institutions in instilling values of tolerance, peace, and human fraternity among youth while rejecting hatred, racism, and violence. The document also calls for updating national legislation to combat hate crimes, extremism, and terrorism and empowering national parliaments to adopt peaceful mediation mechanisms for resolving social conflicts and condemning incitement. Under the declaration, member states are urged to form parliamentary working groups and standing committees to advance interfaith dialogue, coordinate between religious bodies and civil society, and ensure school curricula are free from extremist, racist, or sectarian incitement while integrating human rights and coexistence principles into educational programs. The text further emphasizes directing scientific research toward examining the root causes of ethnic and sectarian conflicts, expanding cultural and artistic exchange across the Arab world, and leveraging media platforms to counter hate speech. It specifically stresses combating the misuse of digital technology and artificial intelligence to defame religions or spread hatred, alongside engaging civil society, women, and youth through public-private partnerships. Arab League Assistant Secretary-General and Head of the Social Affairs Sector Ambassador Mohammed bin Duaij Al Khalifa stated that fostering a culture of tolerance and dialogue is essential for mutual understanding, respect for diversity, and sustainable development. He stressed, however, that tolerance does not mean relinquishing legitimate rights or tolerating occupation and aggression, adding that lasting peace requires justice, adherence to international law, the protection of Palestinian rights, and the establishment of an independent Palestinian state with East Jerusalem as its capital. fde4ffa4a0.title: Morocco AI ministry plans open model as 2026 spending lags
fde4ffa4a0.summary: The Morocco AI ministry, created in October, plans to release the country’s first national open-source language model, adapted to Moroccan Arabic (Darija) and later Amazigh, a parliamentary committee report on its 2027 budget shows. The plan puts language technology at the centre of Morocco AI policy, but the same report shows the ministry had committed only 6.31% of its 2026 credits by mid-October, raising questions about how fast it can spend. Ahmed Rahhou, minister of artificial intelligence, digital transformation and administrative reform, presented the ministry’s first budget to the interior committee of the House of Representatives on 10 November, Express TV reported . Rahhou, formerly head of the Competition Council, joined the government formed in October; a decree on 26 October gave him responsibility for national AI policy, Médias24 reported . The committee’s written report, seen by the Arabic-language news site Hespress and reported on Monday, says Morocco expects to issue “the first open-source national language model”, with early trials to adapt a model to Darija, a Moroccan benchmark for evaluating models and a model to read Moroccan Arabic manuscripts. Quotes are translated from Arabic. The work draws on national datasets that include about 300mn text tokens, 150 gigabytes of documents, 10,000 hours of transcribed Darija audio, the official gazette archive from 1913 to 2026 and about 90,000 legal texts, according to the report. The ministry’s predecessor worked with the French company Mistral AI on open-source tools for Darija under the “Maroc IA 2030” roadmap, the government portal Maroc.ma said . The committee report says that partnership produced an open speech-recognition model. For Morocco AI in public services, the ministry’s “Idarati” assistant, built on about 2,800 administrative procedures and analysis of some 10,000 legal texts, is to gain a voice version and an agent that follows a citizen’s request through to the result. Amazigh support will be added to a meeting assistant that already transcribes Darija. A legal assistant and a guide for entrepreneurs are also planned. On Morocco AI infrastructure, the report lists the Al Jazari data centre, a “digital Igoudar” project in Dakhla, a computing platform with Core Nexus Systems targeting 36 megawatts, and two Oracle cloud regions worth about 1.4bn dirhams ($150mn), the first of them in Casablanca due to start operating in 2026. He stressed that the country must ensure that AI solutions address the needs of citizens and businesses while supporting economic development. The government’s approach will follow King Mohammed VI’s call, in his speech at the opening of the current parliamentary year, for a new generation of national strategies in areas such as the digital economy and artificial intelligence. Rahhou said the ministry will prioritize the implementation of the national “AI Made in Morocco” roadmap alongside the broader “Morocco Digital 2030” strategy, with particular attention to projects that produce measurable results for the economy, public institutions, and society. Morocco prepares workforce for AI-driven changes One of the government’s main challenges will be to help Moroccan workers adapt to the changes that AI could bring to the labor market. Rather than view the technology solely as a threat to existing jobs, Rahhou argued that Morocco should use it to create new professional opportunities, improve productivity, and strengthen existing occupations. The ministry will coordinate with different sectors to identify professions most vulnerable to AI-driven changes and determine which skills workers will need as the technology becomes more widespread. This assessment will inform new continuous training and professional retraining programs to help employees adapt to changing workplace requirements. A Stocktwits headline said the stock gained after Gemini joined Meta, OpenAI and xAI in Oracle’s AI model lineup, and the line spread quickly across finance feeds. This analysis separates what Oracle’s own documentation confirms from what the headline implies. The lineup itself is documented in detail. The link between that lineup and any move in the share price is not. Readers who track the AI spending cycle, which we covered in our look at AI capex and market doubts , should treat the model list as a product fact and the stock reaction as a claim that still needs evidence. Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. Oracle’s official documentation lists four model families as available through OCI Generative AI. They are Google Gemini, Meta Llama, OpenAI GPT and xAI Grok. Each family appears with named model identifiers, which means a developer can read the catalog and pick a specific model string instead of guessing what “access to Gemini” means in practice. The Google entries are Google Gemini 2.5 Pro, Google Gemini 2.5 Flash and Google Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite. The Meta entries are meta.llama-3.3-70b-instruct, meta.llama-4-maverick-17b-128e-instruct-fp8 and meta.llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct. The OpenAI entries include openai.gpt-oss-20b, openai.gpt-oss-120b, GPT-5.3-codex, GPT-5.4-nano and GPT-6-luna. The xAI entries include Grok 4.1 Fast and, reportedly, Grok 4.7, which became available on demand in November 2026. One detail matters for anyone writing about this as a launch. Oracle’s documentation shows that Gemini models are available. It does not establish that Gemini “joined” on a particular date. The sources we reviewed carry no announcement date, no pricing and no customer counts for the lineup. So the accurate framing is that Gemini sits in the catalog today, and the timing of its arrival stays unconfirmed in this reporting. The count of 18 reflects the identifiers in the documentation we relied on. 862f2dd495.title: Import AI 481: AI sub-contractors; a wet lab for AI; and subterfuge during development
862f2dd495.summary: Welcome to Import AI, a newsletter about AI research. Import AI runs on arXiv, cappuccinos, and feedback from readers. If you’d like to support this, please subscribe. Subscribe now AI systems are getting good at sub-contracting to make themselves better: …AI can now productively spend money to improve itself… Researchers have developed FrontierML, a benchmark “that measures how well agents turn capital into model performance on challenging, end-to-end machine learning tasks.” It shows that today’s frontier systems are already able to, when given some money, turn this into improving their own performance on a basket of 21 distinct tasks. 21 long-horizon tasks “inspired by real work at frontier labs, neolabs, and academic institutions”. These tasks span six category areas, including LLM training, efficiency, vision & audio, computer use, applied NLP, and math & games. “Each task provides the agent with the same setup: a 12-hour CPU sandbox, a wallet with $10, $50, or $200, a few validation samples, and a task description.” Example task: Agents try to solve the tasks in pretty different ways. E.g, for one task about generating screenshots, the top-scoring agent fine-tuned a diffusion model using LoRA, while other high-scoring approaches involved an LLM writing a drawing program that is then rendered. Key features: Scaling spending : “Give agents $10, $50, and $200 per task to spend on training compute and data, and evaluate whether agents can use the additional capital productively,” they write. “In our experiments, we find that stronger agents are able to reliably improve their submissions with greater access to capital.” Open-ended & end-to-end : “In each task, agents can choose architectures, source data, implement training, provision compute, evaluate checkpoints, and optimize inference,” they write. One notable observation is that agents do quite a lot of novel stuff; “in 28% of trajectories, agents add newly trained parts to pretrained models or train a new model from scratch.” Decent verification: “Agents submit an inference server that serves their model on an air-gapped H100 machine,” they write. “To disincentivize overfitting, we provide limited validation samples and evaluate on a large out-of-distribution held-out test set, not shown to the agent”. Results : The authors measure performance by looking at the change in mean score over the 21 tasks when given additional money. Their baseline is a human researcher, which is able to get a 56 point…

883e769439.title: Microsoft outage cause revealed: It was a perfect storm of problems
883e769439.summary: You're probably aware that Microsoft 365, the popular suite of products that includes Outlook, suffered a massive global outage last week. In fact, it was the worst outage of the year , by a sizable margin. The problem took the computer giant roughly 24 hours, over the course of two business days , to get everything back up and running. Aside from wondering when their email would be working again , the number one question on everyone's mind was what in the world happened to keep Microsoft 365 down for so long? Now, we know. In a statement shared with customers and on X, Microsoft explained there were actually three causes, which created a perfect storm. First, a bug caused servers to become unresponsive in specific conditions; second, an issue with Microsoft Teams increased server traffic and created those conditions; and third, many additional servers were already offline from an unrelated issue. As Microsoft explained, on their own, neither issue would have caused such a large-scale problem. However, together, well, they kept one of the world's biggest tech companies scrambling for two days to fix their service. In a social media post published on X, Microsoft's EVP of Copilot, Agents, and Platform Charles Lamanna explained the situation in detail. According to Lamanna, a "latent defect" resulted in the company's servers becoming "overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions." The defect that caused the problem was introduced to Microsoft's systems during a July 2026 update as part of a fix for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers. For months, as Lamanna described it, the issue went undetected, and it didn't cause any problems under normal load during Microsoft's testing process. The second problem occurred when a surge in server load set off the defect. Lamanna says that Microsoft maintains two independent network gateway systems for Microsoft 365 to handle outages and disruptions. However, 15 hours before the global Microsoft 365 outage, Teams "failed over" from the alternative networking gateway to the primary one, which supports Exchange Online . Finally, Microsoft's servers weren't operating at 100 percent at the time. According to Lamanna, it just so happened that nearly 14 percent of the server capacity for the networking gateway was out of service…

60dce247cf.title: Major tech outages with Microsoft, FAA, and banking systems expose digital vulnerabilities
60dce247cf.summary: RALEIGH, N.C. (WTVD) -- A series of technology disruptions affecting air travel , banking, and other critical systems is raising questions about how dependent everyday life has become on digital infrastructure and the vulnerabilities that come with it. Chase Bank said technical problems affecting its systems Monday were caused by a software bug, not a cyberattack. Other banks also reported similar issues. The banking problems followed other recent disruptions, including an issue involving Microsoft on Thursday and the Federal Aviation Administration on Friday. There is no indication the banking problems are connected to last week's Microsoft outage. The string of disruptions has left some people questioning the reliability of the systems they use every day. "We're not sure what's happening with our digital infrastructure, " Katie Caceres said. Caceres was in Raleigh for a conference and said she barely made it because of flight delays. She also expressed skepticism about explanations for the recent disruptions. "I don't know if I really believe the explanation that has been given," Caceres said. "Growing up with systems that we've been told to trust but aren't really working anymore has been not great," she continued. Technology now plays a role in everything from accessing money and catching a flight to operating vehicles and home security systems. Cybersecurity experts say those systems can be hacked and that increasing dependence on technology creates more vulnerabilities. Kimberely Simon, a cybersecurity strategist and CEO of Growth Office Partners, said cybercriminals have the ability to target large numbers of people quickly. "Cybercrime is able to attack people in the masses today, by the second, by the minute," Simon said. "They are attacking and trying to trick thousands and thousands and millions of people. So today, cybersecurity is just one of those things that you cannot ignore. Nobody is safe" Simon said the recent outages are concerning but cautioned against assuming every technology failure is connected to criminal activity. "I think one thing people need to realize is that not every outage is a cyberattack. So, when an outage happens, you need investigators who come and tell you what happened. Is it because of a criminal attack? But sometimes it really is equipment stopped working or a system failed." 84fb456dba.title: Microsoft reveals how July software bug triggered global outage
84fb456dba.summary: Hidden defect left over 80% of affected gateway servers unresponsive Dubai: Microsoft has revealed that a software bug introduced in July was a major factor behind last week’s global Microsoft 365 outage, which disrupted Outlook, Teams and other services for nearly 24 hours. In a preliminary report released after the November 12-13 disruption, the company said the defect had gone undetected for more than three months before increased network traffic and reduced server capacity triggered widespread failures. At the height of the incident, more than 80 per cent of Microsoft’s affected networking gateway servers became unresponsive in less than two hours. The disruption affected access to Outlook and Exchange Online, delaying emails and interrupting services used by businesses and organisations worldwide, including in the UAE. Microsoft identified three contributing factors: a software defect dating back to July, increased traffic following a Microsoft Teams network failover, and an unrelated problem that had already taken nearly 14 per cent of the affected gateway’s server capacity offline. The July update had been deployed globally without apparent problems. However, under certain traffic conditions, the defect caused servers to become overwhelmed and stop responding. About 15 hours before the outage, Microsoft Teams switched to networking infrastructure also used by Exchange Online, increasing the load on those systems. With part of the server capacity already unavailable, the additional traffic triggered the previously undetected defect. As servers stopped responding, Microsoft’s systems automatically redirected traffic to other servers. Those servers then became overloaded, causing failures to spread across the network. Microsoft said its testing had failed to reproduce the conditions that eventually triggered the problem. The defect was more likely to occur on newer, more powerful servers with additional processor cores, while the company’s testing largely used less powerful hardware. The combination of increased traffic and reduced capacity exposed the problem during peak US usage hours. Microsoft said restarting affected servers did not immediately restore services because they were overwhelmed again by requests that had accumulated during the disruption. The age of the defect also complicated recovery. Since the problematic code had been deployed months earlier, engineers could not simply reverse a recent update using the company’s normal rollback…

35ad3f1cf9.title: UAE among nine US allies pledging to safeguard sensitive AI technology
35ad3f1cf9.summary: The UAE is among several key US allies pledging to safeguard the most sensitive AI technology they are being given access to. The Emirates was among so-called Pax Silica member countries to sign the San Francisco Declaration. Omran Sharaf , the UAE's assistant foreign minister for advanced science and technology, was among those at the signing ceremony in San Francisco on Sunday. Australia, India, Israel , Japan, South Korea, Qatar, Singapore and the UK were also present at the event held near the Golden Gate Bridge. The declaration came amid a US investigation into the Jensen Huang scandal and allegations he had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, who led the Singapore-based tech firm Megaspeed. On Tuesday, the US Department of Commerce and Department of Justice said it had investigated Megaspeed back in 2025, amid claims it was re-exporting sensitive Nvidia chips to China, which the US has restrictions on. “The declaration affirms that economic security is fundamental to national security, sets out the participants’ common understanding of the sensitive technologies and critical infrastructure that underpin Super Intelligence supply chains, and declares that safeguarding them is a shared endeavour,” a news release from the US State Department stated. The State Department adhered to the Trump White House's mandate that the government calls AI “super intelligence”, or SI. The announcement also said Pax Silica, a Trump administration initiative launched in 2025 to secure technology supplies crucial for building AI, would enter a new phase. “No nation can secure the foundations of the SI era alone, and the prosperity SI makes possible will only be as durable as the supply chains and infrastructure beneath it,” the release stated. “By agreeing on what must be protected and committing to protect it together, participants are laying the secure foundations on which partner nations can innovate, invest, and grow.” Jacob Helberg , the undersecretary for economic affairs, reflected on the announcement shortly after attending the signing ceremony. “Defining these foundations together lets us protect them together,” he posted on X. In recent years, concerns about US AI technology potentially being shared with adversarial countries has steadily increased, with some warning that if unchecked, the US lead in AI could evaporate. The declaration refers to sensitive technologies and the importance of protecting all goods, software materials, knowledge…

4b4d3679ce.summary: Megaspeed, the AI infrastructure company linked to the scandal that toppled Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang , has said Alice Huang left the business more than a year ago. “Ms Alice Huang officially left Megaspeed effective August 30, 2025, and currently has no role with the company,” it said in a statement on Sunday. The company said it “conducts legitimate and lawful business” and had “retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation”, including a review of its compliance with US export controls. It said media reports against it were not supported by verifiable evidence. How Nvidia's Veterans Day video inadvertently sealed Jensen Huang's fate amid scandal Megaspeed is suspected of helping Chinese companies get around US restrictions by buying Nvidia’s advanced chips for data centres in South-East Asia and routing them to China. Singapore authorities have said servers containing advanced AI chips were shipped to Malaysia and may have been delivered elsewhere, contrary to declarations made in Singapore. Singapore police said their investigation is continuing. 109886c39d.title: Google AI agents audit Signal’s code and one major flaw stays hidden
109886c39d.summary: Google DeepMind researchers say their AI agents produced mathematical proofs linking specific security guarantees to a compiled build of Signal’s encryption library, and they put the resulting evidence online for others to check. The Nov. 10 AlphaProof Code report describes about 6.5 million lines of machine-checked Lean proof code. The result concerns a particular build of libsignal, the Signal protocol’s implementation, under explicit assumptions about cryptography and the environment in which the code runs. The authors say five people worked on the proofs over four weeks. Humans directed the work, selected reference models and reviewed the specifications that defined what the agents had to prove . The target was an AArch64 Linux executable using libsignal-protocol v0.105.4 and SPQR v1.6.0 inside a small command-line harness. The theorems cover session initialization, sending a message, and receiving one. Key generation falls outside that verified scope. The Google report connects the compiled executable to specified properties of PQXDH and Triple Ratchet one-to-one messaging, including forward secrecy, authentication, and post-compromise security. These address whether earlier messages stay secret after keys are stolen, whether senders are authentic, and whether a session can regain secrecy after a compromise. Its two proof models provide different assurances: the symbolic analysis relies on idealized cryptographic operations and collision-free executions, while the computational analysis bounds the success of classical attackers under stated cryptographic assumptions. The symbolic proof establishes handshake secrecy under specified later breaks of Diffie-Hellman, but the computational proof does not cover quantum attackers. Group messaging is outside the report’s scope, and the computational model excludes multi-device state. Its bounds also stop providing a useful guarantee at sufficiently large workloads. The results still require trust in Lean’s checking kernel, the specifications reviewed by the researchers, the AArch64 Linux model, and contracts describing selected routines. The project’s Nov. 11 update, merged on GitHub , says ten more library routines were verified, cutting trusted routine hooks from 37 to 27. Those hooks replace execution of selected routines with assumed descriptions of their behavior. The update retains libsignal v0.105.4 but changes the pinned executable. The newer build verifies the machine code for those ten routines…

c179f75d16.title: What AI at work really costs
c179f75d16.summary: As you hand off more work to AI, it’s worth comparing the total costs of the leading options, just like you would any other investment that helps you get work done. Today we’re sharing new research on how those costs compare across the same work, and a closer look at what drives the difference. Microsoft commissioned and funded research with GigaOm on Demystifying the TCO of Enterprise AI , which measured the total cost of ownership of Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise, and Claude Enterprise through hands-on testing in October 2026. Microsoft ran the testing and cost analysis. GigaOm contributed to the research design, validated the methodology, results, and cost analysis, and co-developed the findings. The headline is that, on the study’s modeled workloads, Copilot had the lowest estimated monthly cost for both everyday and advanced AI users, while quality was broadly comparable across all three products on the tasks tested. The research modeled two kinds of AI users. Everyday users rely on AI across their workday for tasks like finding information, preparing for meetings, analyzing data, and creating content. Advanced users do all of that and also hand off complex, multi-step work to agents that run on their own. The evaluation covered 37 unique prompts across Copilot Chat and Cowork, plus Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Over a modeled month, that represented 100 tasks for an everyday AI user and 140 for an advanced AI user, including 20 agentic workflows. Each product was tested against the same fictional company and underlying data, with prompts run repeatedly to account for variation in AI responses. You can find the full testing methodology in the report. For the everyday AI user, Copilot costs $30 a month. Claude costs $205 and ChatGPT costs $81, once usage charges were added to their subscriptions. That’s more than 6x and 2.5x Copilot’s cost, respectively. For the advanced AI user, Copilot cost $96 a month. Claude cost $299 and ChatGPT cost $149. That’s more than 3x and 1.5x Copilot’s cost, respectively. Mr Burnham will be in Brussels for a UK-EU summit to seal a new set of accords to align with the bloc’s economy in areas such as agricultural exports. In his signature foreign policy push, Mr Burnham insists his EU reset is a “win-win” for both sides and something closer to the type of Brexit that people assumed was on the table when they voted to leave in 2016. What he is actually doing is setting off an information-sphere battle that could easily subsume his premiership in one of the biggest narrative battles anywhere on the planet. Mr Burnham has displayed strong social media cut-through during his time in office, especially to the types of domestic voters that he wants on his side. The argument attributed to him, that he ultimately wants the UK back in the EU , is a tough sell to bring many of these with him. One survey at the weekend said that the majority of Labour party MPs will face voters that backed the drive to leave the EU a decade ago. The Prime Minister nevertheless says a longer-term convergence with the EU is in the UK’s interest. He describes the current situation on the departure from the EU like the emperor’s new clothes in the children’s fable. Giving his main foreign policy speech of the year on Monday, Mr Burnham asserts that the UK has lost more than it gained in the way that it left the EU. Already a campaign group has formed called Stay Out. It has recycled one of the hardest-hitting punchlines from the last campaign. Then the opponents of the EU said that £350 million ($462 million) a week was going to Brussels, now the figure is projected at more than £750 million. Recycled attacks lines are one thing, but where Mr Burnham faces his biggest fight is with AI-generated misinformation. The EU’s impact on the cost of living is one fruitful area of the headlines that make the raw material for bot-driven content. One newspaper last week suggested that even the starter deal that Mr Burnham is to secure on Friday will result in the UK adopting “two EU laws” a week to align with EU regulations. The fight has thus begun, even though – for the moment – Mr Burnham adheres to the 2024 Labour party manifesto that pledged no re-entry to the EU’s customs union, single market or freedom of movement . 5bfd396c6d.title: Anthropic IPO: For hundreds of billions of dollars flowing into AI startups, a big debut is a must
5bfd396c6d.summary: Artificial intelligence has propelled big gains in venture capital funds this year, and a flood of money — over $350 billion — into AI startups. Venture funds were up close to 18% through the first half of 2026, with 86% of U.S.-based VC investor money going into AI companies. With Anthropic set to make its public market debut this week at a reported valuation of $1.4 trillion — though sources told CNBC on Tuesday the pricing may be upped — the market's reception to the deal and early trading in its shares may set the tone for the next leg in the private market AI boom. It has been a period of increased volatility for tech stocks and the public market AI trade. In addition to concerns about balance sheet strength and valuation, midterm elections showed widespread public opposition to data centers , and the CEO scandal rocking Nvidia, the "central bank" of AI financing , has compounded risks in the sector. But on the private side of tech investing, firms are closely watching how investors react to Anthropic's IPO. "I think that will end up guiding further intentions for the VC space," said Mike McLelland, managing director of investments within private markets at Cleveland, Ohio-based Clearstead. The round was co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, alongside Andreessen Horowitz, with investment from Alphabet , Google's parent. The fresh funds will help fund the design and development of new medicines using AI. Drug discovery startups have seen record funding poured into them by investors in 2026 as companies look to capitalize on advances in AI. OpenAI and Anthropic have also been investing in tools to develop new medicines using the technology. Hassabis has been CEO of Isomorphic Labs since the startup spun out of DeepMind in 2021. "When we founded Isomorphic, our conviction was that biology could be understood and modelled at the most fundamental molecular level and radically accelerated through AI," said Hassabis. "This round enables us to accelerate our progress: building foundational biology models, deepening our systemic disease understanding, and driving our first therapeutic programs towards clinical trials to deliver tangible impact for patients," he added. Isomorphic is building a proprietary drug design engine and therapeutic candidate pipeline designed with AI, which it says will help it deliver the next generation of medicines. Anthropic announced it was launching an AI drug discovery program in June and OpenAI partnered with Novo Nordisk in April. Drug discovery startups have raised $23.2 billion in 2026, according to deal-counting platform Dealroom, a record figure. Isomorphic last raised in May, with a $2.1 billion Series B.

0522f60005.title: Tomorrow.io gives Google DeepMind's WeatherNext 2 and Microsoft's Aurora 1.5 a better start
0522f60005.summary: BOSTON, Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AI weather models can generate global forecasts in minutes, but they still need an estimate of the current atmosphere for initialization. Many rely on conventional data assimilation systems that typically update the starting picture every six hours. Tomorrow.io's Sky 1 uses machine-learning data assimilation to update initial conditions hourly, incorporating fresh observations from our constellation of 15 microwave sounders. These instruments sense atmospheric temperature and moisture, including through clouds, adding observations over oceans and other sparsely monitored regions. In 28 test cases, adding Tomorrow.io's observations reduced initial-state water-vapor error by approximately 5–8% compared with Sky 1 without them, using ERA5, a reconstruction of past weather, as the reference. These improved initial conditions also benefited forecasts from leading AI weather models. Across 112 forecasts from Aurora 1.5 initialized by Sky 1, the observations lowered average near-surface temperature error at weather stations at every evaluated lead time through five days. Forecast gains were modest and strongest in the first two days. A similar pattern was observed in Google DeepMind's WeatherNext 2 with the sounders assimilated. Started from Sky 1 instead of raw GFS data, Aurora 1.5 gained about a day of lead time on near-surface temperature, scored against ERA5. Through Sky 1, the growing fleet and improved instrument calibration are being evaluated across leading AI weather models, including their impact on hurricane tracks, atmospheric river landfalls and severe weather outbreaks. By providing updated initial conditions every hour, Sky 1 enables these fast-running models to bring newly observed atmospheric changes into the next forecast sooner. b0a12233cb.title: Outages at banks, airlines, Microsoft raise security concerns
b0a12233cb.summary: During the past five days, major system crashes have disrupted email, air travel, and banking services in Massachusetts and across the country, raising concerns about digital security and how prepared companies and individuals are for such events. The disruptions began Thursday when Microsoft Outlook crashed , shutting down email access for millions of businesses. On Friday, an air traffic control crisis caused travel disruptions that lasted through the weekend . By Monday, several of the nation’s largest banks reported major outages . All systems are now back online, but experts say it is difficult to determine exactly what is happening. Consumers, however, are particularly alarmed when disruptions involve their money. "Anything that touches money is the most concerning," one expert said. "Not to be conspiratorial, but when too many things happen at the same time, it’s difficult not to be." In the latest outage, Chase Bank reported that a software bug in its hardware system caused the disruption, which affected online banking. As of Monday night, transactions were processing normally again, and the bank confirmed the outage was not the result of a cyberattack. MIT Information and Technologies Professor Stuart Madnick said the recent outages highlight how unprepared companies and individuals can be when critical services fail. "We as individuals need to realize these things can happen, whether it’s by accident or on purpose, and put in place preparations for what we would do if something happens," Madnick said. Experts recommend using multi-factor authentication, avoiding the reuse of passwords, and keeping some emergency cash on hand to protect against potential disruptions. The Chase outage primarily affected its customers, as well as customers at other banks attempting transactions with Chase. However, the issue has been resolved.

"They're pushing new technology on top of really old computer systems, and it just seems to overwhelm the system a little bit, and it's not able to catch up. But it has nothing to do with cyberattacks," he added. Gregory Falco, a Cornell University assistant professor of aerospace and systems engineering, said Mullin's explanation is possible but questioned whether it accounts for all the recent outages. "That doesn't happen for all of these systems overnight. So I think it has to be something a little deeper than that," Falco said. Falco cautioned that he could only speculate about the cause of the disruptions but raised the possibility of Iranian cyberattacks. "Iran has gotten really good at getting in some deep network somewhere. I think we shouldn't discount that," Falco said. b744f28327.title: Meth replaces Captagon as Syria's drug trade collapses, UN warns
b744f28327.summary: Methamphetamine is taking hold across the Middle East as drug gangs move to fill the gap left by the collapse of Syria's Captagon trade, a senior UN official has warned. The end of the war in Syria ruined production of Captagon and broke up the smuggling networks that had flooded the region with the illegal pills, said Siri Bjune of the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC). But crime gangs have been quick to switch products. “The end of the conflict in Syria has disrupted Captagon production and weakened the networks that sustained the market, while methamphetamine is increasingly becoming entrenched in the Near and Middle East,” Ms Bjune told the World Police Summit in Dubai on Tuesday. UAE and Iraq thwart plan to smuggle 200,000 Captagon pills into Ras Al Khaimah Syria was the world's biggest source of Captagon under Bashar Al Assad, whose regime fell in December 2024. Much of the trade was aimed at consumers in the Gulf. Ms Bjune, chief of UNODC's border management branch, said the shift demonstrated how quickly criminal groups can react to pressure from police and changes in the market. Ms Bjune was presenting the UN's World Drug Report 2026 , which found that 331 million people worldwide used drugs in 2024, a rise of 34 per cent from a decade earlier. “Drug use has reached historically high levels,” she told those gathered at Dubai World Trade Centre. Methamphetamine remains the world's largest synthetic drug market. North America, East Asia and South-East Asia are still its biggest markets but smugglers are increasingly pushing it into new regions, including the Middle East. “Traffickers are diversifying their routes, exploiting smaller ports, new transit corridors and sophisticated technologies to move drugs across borders,” Ms Bjune said. She also warned that the Taliban's ban on opium production in Afghanistan appeared to be weakening. Cultivation has risen more than fourfold in a year, from about 10,000 hectares in 2025 to more than 43,000 hectares this year, though figures remain below pre-prohibition levels. Opium has generated an estimated $525 million for traffickers in Afghanistan so far in 2026, she said. The report also raised concerns over fentanyl in North America, the misuse of the painkiller tramadol in parts of Africa and the spread of nitazenes, a group of highly potent synthetic opioids. 5056a13256.title: 'Essentially unusable': OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol to negative reception from AI power users
5056a13256.summary: OpenAI released its new AI models GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol on Tuesday , both with new high benchmark scores and the former with a 20% price cut over the application programming interface (API) — so why are the new models drawing sharp criticism from several AI power users who tested them before launch? Investor and former HyperWrite AI CEO Matt Shumer said he won't be releasing a longer written review as he has customarily done for other preceding OpenAI flagships. The new models "were essentially unusable,” Shumer wrote in a post on X. Developer and YouTuber Theo Browne also posted on X that 6.2 Astra was "the worst model OpenAI has ever released,” he wrote. They singled out the model's shortcomings in delegated work and creative tasks. Wharton professor Ethan Mollick had a more mixed experience with Astra. It built a playable space elevator in Blender and Unity, but he found the model “very uneven & weird” and harder to steer than rival models. Astra now costs $8 per million uncached input tokens and $40 per million output tokens while GPT-6.2 Sol keeps its predecessor 6.1 Sol’s $2 input and $10 output rates. Both are proprietary, hosted models. They’re available now in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users, and through the OpenAI API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol . OpenAI is positioning Astra for assignments such as changing a complex codebase, building a working web application, or producing a document that follows a company’s templates. Sol is the cheaper option for routine coding, writing, and workflows that require several steps. The release comes eight days after rival Anthropic, in the run-up to going public , launched the well-reviewed Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 , also at $8 and $40 per million standard input and output tokens, and a week after Google opened access to its own well-received Gemini 4 Carbon at introductory rates equal to Sol’s. In other words, the competition is intensifying and it's probably one of the worst times for OpenAI to fumble, especially on the reception of its new flagship and middle-tier model. Dan Shipper, CEO of generative AI publication Every , said his team spent several weeks testing both models. He said Astra performed about as well as its predecessor on most of Every’s coding benchmarks, but often stopped early on end-to-end builds. He found that its push for brevity could make writing hard to follow or leave out necessary explanation. He praised its default design…

c4da92541f.summary: Anthropic's blockbuster initial public offering is set to launch on Thursday, a milestone that will test investor enthusiasm for the company behind the popular Claude chatbot and the burgeoning artificial intelligence sector. "This is a case where the deal is so large and important, so central to the AI thesis, that it's going to be a turning point for the AI sector," Matthew Kennedy, a senior market strategist at investment bank Renaissance Capital, told CBS News. "Even non-AI companies are going to feel the ripple effects, especially in the IPO market." Anthropic shares are scheduled to start trading on the Nasdaq stock exchange under the ticker symbol "ANT" after markets open Thursday at 9:30 a.m. EST. In its most recent regulatory filing, San Francisco-based Anthropic said it will offer 825 million shares priced at between $70 and $78, which is expected to raise up to $64.3 billion. The company also plans to raise an additional $26 billion from a slate of other companies, including chipmaker AMD, chip infrastructure provider Broadcom, Google, Microsoft and Nvidia, all of which have a stake in the AI race. Anthropic is expected to formally set its stock price on Wednesday night. "A price above the initial range would point to stronger-than-anticipated demand, while a price cut would signal that the company struggled to find buyers at the level it hoped for," analysts at Renaissance Capital, which tracks IPOs, said in a research note. The market debut is expected to value Anthropic at up to $1.4 trillion, short of the $2 trillion valuation that some IPO experts projected earlier this year. Still, the AI developer — which launched only in 2021 — is on track to stage what could become the second-largest IPO ever. Elon Musk's SpaceX, which raised $75 billion and was valued at roughly $1.7 trillion when it went public in June , currently holds that mark for the largest IPO. Kennedy thinks Anthropic shares will price at the high end, at around $78, and reach $100 by the end of their first day of trading, an increase that would represent a "solid pop," he said. If the stock rises closer to $140, "that would tell me that AI enthusiasm has come roaring back," he added. Although many investors appear eager to own a piece of Anthropic, the IPO comes amid growing concerns about whether the torrid spending on AI will deliver the expected productivity and profit boom. 2209ff09f7.summary: In our latest installment of the Ask a Scientist series, a Google DeepMind research scientist explains the potential behind our AlphaGenome and AlphaGenome Atlas tools. Your browser does not support the audio element. Your genome is your body’s instruction manual: the blueprint that informs how your body functions. It contains 3 billion base pairs of DNA. Because this DNA is responsible in part for switching genes on and off, it could be the difference between developing a disease and avoiding one. Determining which DNA changes cause diseases (and other outcomes) is like finding a needle in a haystack. Illustrative. Your genome, one point at a time. Decoding the DNA sequence is the goal behind AlphaGenome , a model from Google DeepMind. AlphaGenome can take a partial DNA sequence of 1 million base pairs in length, and make thousands of predictions. By comparing these predictions for DNA changes, scientists can find that needle faster. We talked to Google DeepMind research scientist Žiga Avsec to learn more. ŽA: I’m a research scientist overseeing our genomics initiative. Basically, I lead a team that builds models to help us better understand the genome. How is your team making it easier for scientists to predict and understand diseases? It really all comes down to how the genome works. It contains 3 billion DNA base pairs. And each pair contains two bases, which we call “letters.” These letters — A (adenine), T (thymine), C (cytosine), G (guanine) — act like a biological alphabet, spelling out the genetic instruction manual that makes someone who they are. Since you can replace any of those letters with three other letters, there are 9 billion possible single-letter changes. Many genetic diseases are caused by just one of these letters changing. But scientists don’t have time to run billions of studies to figure out which changes make a difference. So we used AlphaGenome to predict the outcomes of all 9 billion single-letter changes, and we created a massive dataset — AlphaGenome Atlas — so scientists can decide what to research faster. Illustrative. The letters are invented for this example. What’s holding scientists back from better understanding the genome? While science can read all 3 billion base pairs of human DNA, we still haven’t fully deciphered the semantics of the genetic code — particularly the non-coding "dark matter" that regulates gene expression and disease risk. Today at Microsoft Ignite, Salesforce and Microsoft announced Copilotforce, a partnership bringing Salesforce to Microsoft’s expansive enterprise productivity ecosystem, alongside new integrations across Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Teams, and Microsoft Fabric. Separately, bidirectional zero-copy capabilities connect Salesforce Data 360 and Microsoft Fabric without duplicating datasets, allowing organizations to query Fabric data natively within Data 360 and securely share Data 360 intelligence into Fabric. These capabilities build on Sales Cloud in Teams, which brings Salesforce CRM insights and workflows into Microsoft Teams, introduced at Dreamforce and currently in pilot. Together, the integrations will allow sellers to prep for meetings in Copilot or Teams, or update supported opportunity details in Teams. “Through Copilotforce, we’re bringing Salesforce to the largest surface in enterprise software today, embedding trusted Salesforce context and intelligent sales workflows directly where sellers work. 340ddf2d74.title: Ignite 2026: Microsoft Makes Copilot the Center of the Office Experience
340ddf2d74.summary: Microsoft is transforming Copilot from an AI assistant into the primary workspace for creating documents, analyzing data, and coordinating projects across Microsoft 365. For enterprises, the shift could reduce the time employees spend switching between applications, but it also places greater importance on governance, data access controls, and oversight of AI-generated content. Microsoft has just announced a major vision for the future of Office at Ignite 2026, which positions the platform as a “human-led, agentic system of work” rather than a collection of standalone productivity applications. This announcement addresses a growing challenge for enterprises as employees increasingly jump between AI chat interfaces, documents, spreadsheets, presentations, meetings, and email threads, which causes context switching and fragmented workflows. Microsoft argues that traditional productivity tools are struggling to keep pace with these increasingly connected work patterns. According to Microsoft, this fragmentation leads to lost productivity and slower decision-making. Employees often spend significant time moving information between apps, rebuilding context, locating files, and coordinating with colleagues across different systems. As organizations adopt AI assistants, the risk of creating another disconnected tool layer increases as well. Microsoft believes enterprises need AI that can follow work across applications and maintain context throughout the entire lifecycle of a project. To address these challenges, Microsoft is bringing core Office capabilities directly into the Microsoft Copilot experience. Office in the Copilot app is now generally available, which allows users to generate and edit Word documents, Excel models, and PowerPoint presentations from a Copilot conversation while maintaining collaboration and coauthoring features. Microsoft is also introducing new experiences such as Today, Pages, and Workspaces, which use AI to surface priorities, generate dynamic content, and coordinate team collaboration. Microsoft has also announced industry-specific capabilities such as Copilot for Sales, CRM-connected sales skills, and Copilot in OneNote, which can transform notes into draft documents, spreadsheets, and presentations. All content remains protected by existing OneDrive security and compliance controls.
